topics.title: Gas variables and named gas laws

concepts.title: Pressure measurement and units
concepts.description: Convert between common pressure units (atm, mmHg, torr, Pa, bar) and interpret open-end/closed-end manometer and barometer readings.

concepts.title: Temperature scales and absolute zero
concepts.description: Convert between Celsius and Kelvin (K = °C + 273.15) and explain why gas law calculations require absolute temperature.

concepts.title: Boyle's Law (P–V inverse relationship)
concepts.description: Apply P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant temperature and amount; explain the inverse relationship using particle collision frequency.

concepts.title: Charles's Law (V–T direct relationship)
concepts.description: Use V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ with absolute temperatures for a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure; explain the direct relationship.

concepts.title: Gay-Lussac's Law (P–T direct relationship)
concepts.description: Apply P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂ at constant volume and amount; relate the direct P–T relationship to increased particle kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Avogadro's Law (V ∝ n)
concepts.description: Recognize that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of moles; use V₁/n₁ = V₂/n₂.

concepts.title: Combined Gas Law
concepts.description: Combine Boyle's, Charles's, and Gay-Lussac's laws into P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ for a fixed amount of gas undergoing multiple variable changes.

concepts.title: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures
concepts.description: Calculate total pressure of a gas mixture as the sum of partial pressures; relate partial pressure to mole fraction (Pᵢ = Xᵢ P_total).

concepts.title: Graham's Law of Effusion
concepts.description: Apply rate₁/rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁) to compare effusion/diffusion rates; relate effusion rate to root-mean-square speed.

concepts.title: Standard temperature and pressure (STP)
concepts.description: Define STP as 0 °C (273.15 K) and 1 atm, and recall that one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L at STP.

topics.title: Ideal gas law, stoichiometry, and gas calculations

concepts.title: Ideal gas law equation PV=nRT
concepts.description: Use PV = nRT to relate pressure, volume, moles, and temperature of an ideal gas; identify the conditions where the ideal gas law is applicable.

concepts.title: Universal gas constant R values
concepts.description: Select the appropriate R value (0.08206 L·atm/mol·K, 8.314 J/mol·K, 62.36 L·torr/mol·K) based on the pressure and volume units in a calculation.

concepts.title: Standard molar volume (22.4 L/mol)
concepts.description: Derive the molar volume of an ideal gas at STP (22.4 L/mol) from PV=nRT and apply it in stoichiometric gas volume calculations.

concepts.title: Volume–volume gas stoichiometry
concepts.description: Use Avogadro's law and balanced equations to relate volumes of gaseous reactants and products at constant temperature and pressure.

concepts.title: Mass–volume gas stoichiometry
concepts.description: Convert between mass of a substance and volume of a gas using molar mass and the ideal gas law at non‑STP conditions.

concepts.title: Gas density from ideal gas law
concepts.description: Derive and apply d = PM/RT to calculate gas density at given P and T, or to determine molar mass from density.

concepts.title: Determining molar mass of a gas
concepts.description: Calculate the molar mass of an unknown gas from experimental mass, volume, temperature, and pressure using M = mRT/(PV).

concepts.title: Gas collection over water correction
concepts.description: Correct for water vapor pressure when collecting a gas over water: P_dry gas = P_total − P_H₂O, then use the dry gas pressure in ideal gas calculations.

concepts.title: Partial pressure and mole fraction calculations
concepts.description: Calculate partial pressure from mole fraction and total pressure (Pᵢ = Xᵢ P_total), or find mole fraction from partial pressure data.

topics.title: Kinetic molecular theory and particle behavior

concepts.title: Postulates of kinetic molecular theory
concepts.description: List and explain the five main KMT postulates: particles in constant random motion, negligible volume, elastic collisions, no intermolecular forces, and average KE proportional to temperature.

concepts.title: Temperature and average kinetic energy
concepts.description: Relate absolute temperature to average translational kinetic energy: KE_avg = (3/2)RT per mole and KE_avg = (3/2)k_B T per molecule.

concepts.title: Root-mean-square speed (u_rms)
concepts.description: Calculate u_rms = √(3RT/M) using molar mass in kg/mol; explain why heavier molecules move slower at the same temperature.

concepts.title: Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution
concepts.description: Sketch and interpret the distribution of molecular speeds; predict how temperature and molar mass shift the peak height and distribution width.

concepts.title: Kinetic explanation of Boyle's Law
concepts.description: Use KMT to explain why pressure increases when volume decreases: more frequent wall collisions per unit area at constant temperature.

concepts.title: Kinetic explanation of Charles's Law
concepts.description: Explain with KMT why volume increases with temperature at constant pressure: faster particles strike walls harder, expanding the container until pressure equalizes.

concepts.title: Kinetic explanation of Dalton's Law
concepts.description: Explain why each gas in a mixture behaves independently and contributes to total pressure proportionally to its mole fraction, according to KMT.

concepts.title: Effusion and Graham's Law derivation
concepts.description: Derive Graham's law from u_rms: effusion rate ∝ average speed ∝ 1/√M, and use rate₁/rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁).

concepts.title: Real gases and compressibility factor Z
concepts.description: Use the compressibility factor Z = PV/nRT to quantify deviations from ideality; Z < 1 indicates dominant attractive forces, Z > 1 indicates dominant repulsive forces.

concepts.title: Van der Waals equation
concepts.description: Apply the van der Waals equation (P + a n²/V²)(V – nb) = nRT; interpret a and b as corrections for intermolecular attraction and finite particle volume.

concepts.title: Conditions for ideal gas behavior
concepts.description: Identify that real gases approach ideality at low pressure (large intermolecular distances) and high temperature (high kinetic energy overcomes attractions).

concepts.title: Reaction rate definition
concepts.description: Express average and instantaneous reaction rates using concentration changes over time, e.g., rate = –Δ[A]/Δt, accounting for stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.title: Rate law and reaction order
concepts.description: Write the differential rate law rate = k[A]^m[B]^n, and determine the order with respect to each reactant and the overall order.

concepts.title: Method of initial rates
concepts.description: Determine rate law exponents by comparing initial rates from experiments where one reactant concentration changes while others are held constant.

concepts.title: Rate constant units by overall order
concepts.description: Deduce units of the rate constant k: zero-order (M·s⁻¹), first-order (s⁻¹), second-order (M⁻¹·s⁻¹), etc., from the overall reaction order.

concepts.title: Zero-order integrated rate law
concepts.description: Apply [A] = –kt + [A]₀ and half-life t₁/₂ = [A]₀/(2k) for zero-order reactions; interpret linear [A] vs t plots.

concepts.title: First-order integrated rate law
concepts.description: Use ln[A] = –kt + ln[A]₀ and constant half-life t₁/₂ = 0.693/k; identify linearity in ln[A] vs t graphs.

concepts.title: Second-order integrated rate law (single reactant)
concepts.description: Apply 1/[A] = kt + 1/[A]₀ and half-life t₁/₂ = 1/(k[A]₀) for second-order A → products; identify linear 1/[A] vs t plots.

concepts.title: Graphical determination of reaction order
concepts.description: Determine the order by testing which plot yields a straight line: [A] vs t (zero), ln[A] vs t (first), or 1/[A] vs t (second).

concepts.title: Elementary reactions and molecularity
concepts.description: Classify elementary steps as unimolecular, bimolecular, or termolecular; write rate laws directly from the stoichiometry of an elementary step.

concepts.title: Rate-determining step in mechanisms
concepts.description: Identify the slowest elementary step as the rate-determining step, and confirm that its derived rate law matches the experimentally determined rate law.

concepts.title: Intermediates vs. catalysts in mechanisms
concepts.description: Distinguish reactive intermediates (produced then consumed) from catalysts (not consumed, regenerated); explain why intermediates do not appear in the overall rate law.

concepts.title: Collision theory of reaction rates
concepts.description: Explain that reactions require collisions with energy ≥ activation energy and proper orientation; relate collision frequency to concentration and temperature.

concepts.title: Activation energy and energy profiles
concepts.description: Interpret potential energy diagrams: identify activation energy (Ea), transition state, and enthalpy change (ΔH) for exothermic and endothermic reactions.

concepts.title: Arrhenius equation
concepts.description: Use k = A e^(–Ea/RT) and its linear form ln k = ln A – (Ea/R)(1/T) to calculate activation energy or rate constants at different temperatures.

concepts.title: Temperature effect on reaction rate
concepts.description: Use the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution to explain why a small temperature increase sharply raises the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Ea, accelerating the reaction.

concepts.title: Effect of concentration on reaction rate
concepts.description: Relate increased reactant concentration to higher collision frequency and explain the effect predicted by the rate law; note zero-order independence.

concepts.title: Effect of surface area on rate
concepts.description: Explain that dividing a solid reactant into smaller particles increases exposed surface area, leading to more frequent collisions and a faster reaction rate.

concepts.title: Nature of reactants and reaction rate
concepts.description: Correlate reaction rate with bond strengths, physical state (s, l, g, aq), and whether the reaction is homogeneous or heterogeneous.

concepts.title: Catalysis and activation energy
concepts.description: Define a catalyst as a substance that provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy, speeding the reaction without being consumed.

concepts.title: Homogeneous vs. heterogeneous catalysts
concepts.description: Distinguish homogeneous catalysts (same phase as reactants) from heterogeneous catalysts (different phase); give examples such as enzymes and solid metal surfaces.

concepts.title: Reaction coordinate diagram with a catalyst
concepts.description: Draw and interpret a potential energy diagram showing a catalyzed pathway with a lower activation energy hump while ΔH remains unchanged.

topics.title: Lab methods, graphs, and experimental analysis

concepts.title: Manometer and barometer operation
concepts.description: Read open‑end and closed‑end manometers to determine gas pressure; interpret mercury barometer readings for atmospheric pressure.

concepts.title: Gas volume measurement techniques
concepts.description: Describe the use of gas syringes, eudiometers, and water displacement with graduated cylinders for collecting and measuring gas volumes.

concepts.title: Water displacement and vapor pressure correction
concepts.description: Perform gas collection over water, apply Dalton's law to correct for water vapor pressure, and ensure temperature equilibrium before measuring.

concepts.title: Dumas method for molar mass of a volatile liquid
concepts.description: Determine the molar mass of a volatile liquid by vaporizing it in a flask of known volume, measuring mass, and applying PV = nRT.

concepts.title: Vapor density by direct measurement
concepts.description: Measure the mass of a known volume of gas at controlled T and P to calculate molar mass using M = mRT/PV.

concepts.title: Monitoring reaction progress
concepts.description: Describe methods to follow concentration over time: spectrophotometry (absorbance), titration of aliquots, pressure change (gases), and conductivity.

concepts.title: Initial rates method in the lab
concepts.description: Design experiments to measure initial rates by varying initial concentrations and extracting the instantaneous slope at t = 0 for rate law determination.

concepts.title: Clock reactions for kinetics
concepts.description: Use the iodine clock reaction or similar systems to determine rate by measuring the time until a sudden color change, relating time to initial rate.

concepts.title: Graphical analysis of kinetics data
concepts.description: Create and interpret plots of [A] vs t, ln[A] vs t, and 1/[A] vs t to determine reaction order and extract the rate constant from the linear slope.

concepts.title: Experimental determination of activation energy
concepts.description: Measure rate constants at multiple temperatures, construct an Arrhenius plot (ln k vs 1/T), and calculate Ea from slope = –Ea/R.

concepts.title: Temperature control and quenching techniques
concepts.description: Use water baths or heating blocks for precise temperature regulation; stop a reaction by rapid cooling (quenching) or by adding a quenching reagent.

concepts.title: Error analysis in gas and kinetics experiments
concepts.description: Identify common error sources: gas leaks, incomplete vaporization, temperature fluctuations, timing errors, parallax; calculate percent error and suggest improvements.
